metrics.gate: NOT PASSED: 47 covered, 6 partial, 3 gap, 0 failed

S1.1.title: Peak congestion: queue spillback is detected from the live network state

S1.2.not_shown: the trained forecast is significantly worse than the baseline on the held-out test for the 30-minute density target (ACC-02), so the baseline is what is served there: the prediction is measured, labelled and honest, but it is a weak predictor.
S1.2.title: Peak congestion: the near-future queue is predicted

S1.3.title: Peak congestion: a corridor plan is recommended with benefit, harm and safe bounds

S1.4.title: Peak congestion: a person approves it, a second person, after the policy runs again on what is true now

S1.5.title: Peak congestion: the approved plan is applied to the simulator by the only identity that may execute

S1.6.title: Peak congestion: the improvement is measured independently, and reported as it is

S2.1.title: Collision: safety candidates are raised from telemetry and corroborated by a second source

S2.2.not_shown: the correlator joins sensor modalities (loop, camera, road condition); an emergency CALL is not an input to it (calls are dispatched, not correlated), so 'video, radar and call evidence' are not fused into one incident - a person links a call to an incident.
S2.2.title: Collision: candidates from independent sensor modalities are correlated into one explainable incident

S2.3.title: Collision: the affected lanes are closed through the governed adapter

S2.4.title: Collision: units are dispatched with routes, ETA and uncertainty, and the call follows its unit to cleared

S2.5.not_shown: the variable-message-sign adapter records the message and says so honestly: SUMO has no sign to actuate, so 'the warning was published' is a recorded command, not an observed change on the road.
S2.5.title: Collision: a diversion is issued and a driver message is published to the sign

S2.6.title: Collision: traffic recovery is verified independently of the requester, approver and executor

S3.1.title: Ambulance: a fastest-safe route with ETA and uncertainty from live state, never through a closed segment

S3.2.title: Ambulance: signals are pre-empted along the route with pedestrian clearance preserved

S3.3.title: Ambulance: arrival time is compared with the same run without pre-emption

S3.4.title: Ambulance: staged multi-agency response holds units back until their prerequisite has arrived

S4.1.not_shown: the flood candidate combines the road-condition sensor's flood flag with its friction estimate; rainfall, water depth as a measurement, the speed reduction at loop detectors and reports from people are NOT combined into it.
S4.1.title: Flooding: a flood is detected from the road-condition sensor, corroborated by low friction, contradiction demoted

S4.2.title: Flooding: the flooded segment is treated as closed by routing and diversion

S4.3.not_shown: as S2.5: the sign command is recorded, the simulator shows nothing; no public-alert channel exists or is authorized.
S4.3.title: Flooding: a warning is published

S5.1.not_shown: a controller-reported fault is deliberately NOT a safety candidate, and nothing else raises it: the data-quality detector covers the four numeric device types, not the categorical signal state, and no rule looks for conflicting greens or a stuck phase in the controller's own telemetry. `signal_fault` is an incident type nothing produces.
S5.1.title: Signal failure: inconsistent phase or controller telemetry is detected and raises an incident

S5.2.not_shown: there is no safe-plan action among the governed adapters (signal plan change, diversion, sign, transit priority, pre-emption); a controller fault cannot be answered by the platform.
S5.2.title: Signal failure: the platform enters a safe plan

S5.3.not_shown: the platform has no maintenance work item; an escalated incident waits for a person (P10.08) but nothing is created for a maintenance crew.
S5.3.title: Signal failure: maintenance work is created

S5.4.not_shown: the independent outcome verifier exists for governed actions and reports an unknown outcome honestly; there is no signal-failure action to verify.
S5.4.title: Signal failure: restoration is verified

S6.1.title: Outage: the edge buffers what it senses durably while the uplink is down and keeps working

S6.2.title: Outage: stale state is shown as stale and never used as fresh

S6.3.title: Outage: on reconnect the readings replay in order, acknowledged, without accepted duplicates

S6.4.title: Outage: the central state is reconciled after the outage

S7.1.title: Bad model: degraded predictions are detected as alerts on the running edge runtime

S7.2.title: Bad model: an unverified or tampered model is refused and the baseline serves

S7.3.title: Bad model: the model is rolled back to the previous verified version and health is verified

S7.4.title: Bad configuration: a bad rollout is contained and undone
